mappings.note: Sorrieu's 1848 print of a world of democratic nation-states - the evolution of the nationalist idea, LO-3, not LO-1, since nothing here is about the French Revolution's effect abroad.
What nationalism as a late-19th-century force means - the core of LO-3.
A terminology match (utopia, absolutist, benevolent monarchy). Pure term recall, which is what C-1.1 names; no LO's content is being tested.
Definition of 'plebiscite' - a term, C-1.1, not LO-3, which is about how nation states evolved.
Renan on why nations are necessary - the idea of the nation, LO-3.
Congress of Vienna attendance - the conservative order that the movements of the period rose against, LO-2.
The French Revolution as the source of the nationalist idea - LO-1 exactly.
Statements about the French Revolution and sovereignty passing to the people - LO-1.
The revolutionaries' declared mission to liberate Europe's peoples - LO-1's impact-on-Europe clause.
The Civil Code of 1804 as the Napoleonic Code - LO-1.
Where the Napoleonic Code was exported - LO-1's impact on European countries.
What liberal nationalism stood for - the liberal-nationalist current among the movements of the time, LO-2, rather than the bare term recall of C-1.1.
Mazzini's secret society Young Italy - a movement of the period, LO-2.
Definition of 'universal suffrage' - a term, C-1.1.
Features of conservatism as a concept - C-1.1; LO-2 would be right if it asked how conservatives acted against a movement.
The treaty recognising Greek independence - outcome of the Greek national movement, LO-2.
Metternich's remark on France - the conservative reaction of the period, LO-2.
Poland partitioned out of existence - the nation-state question, LO-3.
Prussia's leading role in German unification - the formation of a nation state, LO-3.
The seven years of Prussian wars completing unification - LO-3.
Kaiser William I proclaimed German emperor, 1871 - LO-3.
Victor Emmanuel II as king of united Italy - LO-3.
How Britain's nation state was formed - LO-3, the 'and elsewhere' clause.
Bismarck as the architect of German unification - LO-3.
Germania, the allegory of the German nation - how the nation was imagined, LO-3.
Ottoman control of the Balkans - the setting of the rivalry LO-4 asks to be evaluated as a cause of the First World War.
The date of the French Revolution - LO-1.
France's political situation in 1789 - LO-1.
The revolutionary idea of a united community under a constitution - LO-1.
The tricolour replacing the royal standard - a French Revolution measure, LO-1.
Election of the Estates General - LO-1.
Estates General renamed the National Assembly - LO-1.
Measures taken in the name of the nation - LO-1.
The centralised administrative system of the Revolution - LO-1.
French made the common language, regional dialects discouraged - a French Revolution nation-building measure, LO-1.
The declared destiny to liberate Europe's peoples - LO-1.
How European cities reacted to the news from France - LO-1's 'impacted European countries'.
Purpose of the Jacobin clubs - LO-1.
What the Jacobin campaigns produced - LO-1.
Where the French armies moved - the export of revolutionary ideas, LO-1.
The idea the armies carried abroad - LO-1.
Napoleon's measures in the territories he held - LO-1.
The nature of Napoleonic rule in France - LO-1.
What Napoleon destroyed in France - LO-1.
Napoleon's rationalising reforms - LO-1.
The Civil Code of 1804 by its other name - LO-1.
What the Civil Code established - LO-1.
Regions the Code was exported to - LO-1's impact on European countries.
Napoleon's rural reforms - abolition of serfdom and manorial dues, LO-1.
Napoleon's urban reforms - guild restrictions removed, LO-1.
Germany, Italy and Switzerland as patchworks of states in the mid-18th century - the starting point LO-3 traces the evolution from.
The date Napoleon invaded Italy - LO-1.
The Habsburg Empire's territories - the dynastic multi-national state against which nation states formed, LO-3, rather than C-1.4, since nothing is read off a map.
Industrialisation in France and the German states - the social change behind the new middle-class movements LO-2 covers.
Definition of liberalism - a concept, C-1.1.
Definition of suffrage - a term, C-1.1.
The franchise restricted to property-owning men in revolutionary France - LO-1.
Customs barriers a merchant crossed in 1833 - the economic fragmentation whose removal made German unification, LO-3.
Formation of the zollverein - LO-3.
What the zollverein did - economic unification feeding the nation state, LO-3.
The date of Napoleon's defeat - LO-1.
Definition of conservatism - a concept, C-1.1.
The Treaty of Vienna and its participants - the restored conservative order, LO-2.
Who Mazzini was and what he did - a movement leader of the period, LO-2.
Metternich's remark - the conservative reaction, LO-2.
The Treaty of Constantinople, 1832 - the Greek national movement's outcome, LO-2.
Louis Philippe's flight and the 1848 Republic - a revolution of the period, LO-2.
Bismarck as chief architect of Prussian-led unification - LO-3.
The three wars completing German unification - LO-3.
The Versailles proclamation of January 1871 - LO-3.
Mazzini's 1830s programme for a unitary Italian republic - his movement, LO-2, matching the other Mazzini items; the unification itself is LO-3.
Victor Emmanuel II proclaimed king of united Italy, 1861 - LO-3.
Garibaldi as the celebrated Italian freedom fighter of unification - LO-3.
The Balkans as the most serious source of tension after 1871 - LO-4, the causes of the First World War.
Great-power rivalry over the Balkans as a major cause of the war - LO-4 verbatim.
Ireland's forcible incorporation into the United Kingdom - the making of the British nation state, LO-3.
